items.title: Replacing creative jobs with AI could have a hidden cost, a new report warns
items.excerpt: D&AD's 2026 AI and Creativity Report finds AI-declared award entries more than doubled year-on-year to 27.6%, while studios quietly cut the junior, repetitive work AI now absorbs. The warning: those tasks are where creative judgement was traditionally trained, so automating them may starve the next generation of design leads.

items.title: The story of China's viral "worst animation ever" just keeps getting weirder
items.excerpt: Niu Lai, mocked online as China's "worst animation ever", turns out to have been made almost entirely by a mother-and-son team, and is now being framed as an anti-AI success story. A case study in how audiences read craft, effort and authorship in a generative era.

items.title: Is the future of software certain once AI is everywhere?
items.excerpt: Argues that "extinction" is the wrong lens for what AI does to conventional software — evolution is the right one — using the 2025 enterprise-software selloff as the starting point. Reframes what product designers should be building when models can assemble the app themselves.

items.title: What The Matrix got right about AI
items.excerpt: Re-reads The Matrix 25 years on as a product roadmap rather than science fiction: the real choice was never the pills, but whether users get to see the system at all. A designer's argument about legibility and consent in AI interfaces.

items.title: AI adoption and the slow erosion of design idealism
items.excerpt: How years of client work, deadlines and professional practice reshape a designer's relationship with emerging technology — and why enthusiasm for AI tooling curdles into resignation. A field note on design-org culture as AI adoption becomes mandatory.

items.title: AI isn't replacing mobile UX designers—it's just saving us from infinite wireframe loops
items.excerpt: A mobile designer's account of where AI actually lands in the workflow: it kills the endless low-fidelity wireframe iteration loop, not the judgement calls. Practical framing of which parts of the mobile UX process are safe to hand to a model.

items.title: Why AI Should Return Interfaces, Not Walls of Text
items.excerpt: Argues that the chat-first default — ask for an outcome, get a wall of prose — is a design failure, and that AI responses should render actual components. A concrete case for generative UI over generative text.

items.title: CSS variables are the only design token format that matters
items.excerpt: A contrarian take on the DTCG/JSON token pipeline: the author argues the JSON-parsing layer between Figma variables and shipped CSS is dead weight, and CSS custom properties should be the source of truth. Directly relevant to teams wiring design systems into AI codegen.

items.title: Onshape is bracing for an AI explosion
items.excerpt: PTC's new FeatureScript MCP server lets any AI coding agent — Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini — build, test and debug custom Onshape CAD features in natural language. Non-developers can now generate the bespoke design tools that previously required a FeatureScript specialist.

items.title: Scaling AI agents is where things get complicated
items.excerpt: Incremental agent deployment is fine as a starting point, but the piece argues serious organizations must treat it as a bridge to deeper process redesign. Relevant to design orgs bolting agents onto existing handoffs instead of rethinking them.

items.title: Humans-in-the-loop is likely the fastest way to AI value
items.excerpt: The more valuable and complex a design or manufacturing process becomes, the more it matters to define exactly where the machine stops and the person takes over. A practical framework for drawing the handoff line in AI-assisted product development.

items.title: Scantic trains 3D Gaussian Splats entirely on your phone
items.excerpt: A new free iOS app generates 3D Gaussian Splat scans of objects and environments entirely on-device, with no cloud processing. Puts neural-radiance-style capture in a designer's pocket for reference, previz and product scanning.

items.title: New CG software you may have missed: 16 August 2026
items.excerpt: CG Channel's fortnightly roundup of smaller DCC, AI-assisted and pipeline tool releases that slipped past the main news cycle. A useful sweep of what shipped for 3D and motion designers over the past two weeks.

items.title: Manually Retopologize Your 3D Meshes with This Blender Tool
items.excerpt: Quad Maker is a new Blender add-on for keeping topology clean by hand — a deliberate counterpoint to the wave of AI auto-retopology tools shipping this year. Worth watching as the manual-versus-generated line in 3D production gets redrawn.

items.title: Artist Shows Soft Body Simulation Made with WIP Blender Add-On
items.excerpt: Alan Syarif's WIP Marrow add-on fills any mesh with a tetrahedral cage and solves neo-Hookean XPBD on the GPU with real volume preservation. Real-time squash-and-stretch physics that motion and product designers can art-direct live.

items.title: How Engineers Use KeyShot to Cut Physical Prototyping Costs
items.excerpt: Physical prototypes cost thousands per iteration; KeyShot lays out how design teams use real-time rendering to decide what is actually worth building before committing to tooling. A concrete cost argument for shifting industrial-design review into the render engine.

items.title: Block's new Apache 2.0 agent workspace Berd works across models and harnesses, stores conversation history locally
items.excerpt: Block open-sourced Berd, a free desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux that gives AI agents roles, skills, tools and recognizable visual identities via personas like Berdy, Pushback and Copycat. A rare look at what deliberate agent-identity design looks like as a shipped product.

items.title: Not every problem needs an AI agent
items.excerpt: The smartest AI system may be the one that knows when not to reach for an agent at all. A restraint argument for teams currently retrofitting agents into every step of a design or product workflow.

items.title: Pico's Vision Pro Competitor Gets Official Name and Debut Date
items.excerpt: Pico's Project Swan standalone headset is now officially the Pico Space Pro, debuting at a Beijing event early next month. A second serious spatial-computing platform means a second set of spatial UI conventions for designers to target.

items.title: HeyGears adds G1X desktop colour resin 3D printer to line-up
items.excerpt: The HeyGears G1X brings full-colour resin 3D printing to the desktop at a sub-£3,000 price point. Colour-accurate physical prototypes on the studio bench shortens the loop between CAD, render and a part you can hand to a client.

items.title: CSS Navigation Matching, Early Days
items.excerpt: An early look at applying styles based on which page a user navigated from, making cross-document view transitions declarative in CSS instead of hand-managed in JavaScript. Moves motion design decisions back into the stylesheet where designers can own them.

items.title: Figma Motion basics: Animation styles
items.excerpt: Figma walks through Motion's preset animation styles, which add motion without manually configuring keyframes. Part of the ongoing push to make prototyping motion a native design-file act rather than a handoff to a separate tool.

items.title: Your New Backup Brain Is Here
items.excerpt: A hands-on look at Memoket AI Gem, an ambient capture tool that catches the follow-ups and half-thoughts you say you'll remember later. Framed as a personal-memory layer for creators managing scattered project context.
